mission.brief: A colleague supplied a fictional cedar-01 sample. Save the first five records of snapshot.txt (context, interval, cpu, memory, io) in baseline.txt; omit the note. Display the original and final report with cat after writing. Self-review: what does this interval establish, and what additional evidence is needed?
constraints: SIMULATOR: supplied synthetic snapshots of fictional hosts, not measurements of your computer or VM. No free, vmstat, df, processes, mounts, repairs or cleanup commands are simulated here.

Score checks factual report bytes, reading evidence and preserved sources only. Interpretation, uncertainty and recommended next checks require self-review; 100/100 is NOT proof of diagnostic mastery.

Type help for supported text commands. For this lab's context, worked interpretation and common mistakes, read HELP.txt with cat. This reference is available in both modes; it contains no repair command.

Only declared report files can be written. > truncates before reading; >> appends. Errors do not undo writes. Finish all report writes before reading sources and final reports: any actual write clears earlier reading evidence.

Keep source record spelling, units, order and final LF exactly in reports. Equivalent supported paths and filters count for report construction. Required reading evidence specifically uses cat on each source and final report after the last write; other tools do not satisfy cat inspections. Reasoning is self-reviewed. Reset preserves history.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR HELP — resource baseline
These are original, synthetic annotated fields, not raw vmstat output.
Reference: procps vmstat, one-second second report. CPU fields are percentages; us+sy+id+wa+st here = 100. Memory uses KiB; bi/bo use KiB/s. The first vmstat CPU/I/O report normally averages since boot; do not mix it with later intervals. Process/memory fields are instantaneous.
Self-review questions: Is 80% idle proof of spare capacity all day? Does wa=5% establish a disk fault? What would you collect next?
Model interpretation: this interval has 15% user+system CPU time, 80% idle and some I/O-wait time. It does not locate a disk fault or prove persistent load. Compare repeated intervals, workload timestamps and device-level observations before diagnosing. No measurement of your machine occurred.
Common mistakes: omitting the host/time or units; confusing rates with totals; assuming CPU percentage is per-core; interpreting one sample as a long-term bottleneck.
Automatically checked: five exact evidence records, source/report readings after the last write, unchanged source. Self-reviewed: explanations and next checks. Type help for the command subset.
Required checked reading actions use cat on each source and final report after the last write. Other text tools may construct reports but do not satisfy these cat actions.
